records.title: PARP1 revisited — integrating DNA repair, replication and therapeutics
records.description: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 (PARP1) is a versatile DNA damage sensor and a major therapeutic target in cancer. This Review discusses emerging insights into how PARP1 recognizes and responds to its varied substates, and the implications of these insights on the use of PARP inhibitors.

records.title: The nucleocytoplasmic actin circuit in genome maintenance
records.description: The authors propose that nuclear actin levels are maintained through a regulatory circuit involving the DNA damage response, condensates, and transcriptional replenishment.

records.title: The integration of protein and organelle degradation systems and its pathophysiological functions
records.description: Removal of defective or excessive proteins and organelles is controlled by the ubiquitin–proteasome system and by autophagy pathways. This Review discusses the interplay between these degradation processes in response to physiological demands and cellular stresses and their pathological relevance.

records.title: Phosphatidylinositol 3,4-bisphosphate is a novel lipid helper for mitochondrial fusion
records.description: Golgi-derived vesicles that contain phosphatidylinositol 3,4-bisphosphate facilitate mitochondrial fusion at sites marked with mitofusins and endoplasmic reticulum.

records.title: Mechanisms and regulation of proteolytic DNA–protein crosslink repair
records.description: DNA–protein crosslinks (DPCs) obstruct essential chromatin processes, and their removal is crucial for genome stability. This Review discusses the origin and properties of DPCs, mechanisms of proteolytic DPC repair, and how defective DPC proteolysis contributes to genome instability, premature ageing and disease.

records.title: Similar small RNAs, different biological outcomes
records.description: Similar small RNAs in Caenorhabditis elegans pair with different Argonaute proteins, resulting in differential targeting of nucleic acids and biological outcomes.

records.title: Molecular functions, cellular responses and pathological implications of the RNA modification N 6 -methyladenosine
records.description: This Review discusses how the RNA modification N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) precisely regulates eukaryotic gene expression and orchestrates cellular stress responses, metabolic homeostasis and immunity. It also explores the pathological consequences of m 6 A dysregulation in brain disorders and cancer.

records.title: Why cells use many lipids when few will do
records.description: A synthetic minimal cell can survive with just two lipids, revealing that extensive lipid diversity is not essential for life. This Comment discusses our current understanding of why cells contain so many lipids and highlights future research avenues.

records.title: Revealing the invisible transcriptome
records.description: The discovery of widespread expression of unstable promoter-associated transcripts has changed our understanding of genomic transcription activity.

records.title: Ubiquitin phosphorylation opens a hatch to a code still largely undeciphered
records.description: The discovery of ubiquitin phosphorylation as a mitophagy activator pointed to ubiquitin being at the heart of a broad signalling code.

records.title: Scaling up measurements of the interactions that build condensates
records.description: Condensate partitioning by mRNA-display (CPmD) enables high-throughput assessment of protein (domain) propensity for condensate formation.

records.title: Atomic, structural and molecular insights into GPCR ligand binding and signalling
records.description: This Review explores the atomic, structural and molecular basis of G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR)-mediated signalling, highlighting recent insights into conformational changes associated with ligand recognition and interaction with downstream adaptors, and underscoring their importance for the development of therapeutics.

records.title: Engineering synthetic proteins to toggle function in response to kinase signals
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Cao (Toettcher Lab) discusses the development of kinase-responsive phospho-switches that enable researchers to couple endogenous kinase signalling to activation of a synthetic protein actuator.

records.title: Towards a systematic understanding of the diverse subtypes, biogenesis and functions of large extracellular vesicles
records.description: Large extracellular vesicle (lEV) subtypes have diverse biogenesis, cargo, functions and roles in disease. This Review article provides an overview of lEV characteristics, highlights open questions in the field and indicates how a systematic approach towards lEV characterization assisted by emerging technologies will ensure reproducibility, advancing lEV research.

records.title: Chaperone-mediated autophagy in physiological homeostasis, disease and ageing
records.description: Chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA) is a selective lysosomal degradation pathway. Recent insights into its regulation, substrate repertoire and therapeutic modulation have revealed organ-specific functions and highlighted CMA as a therapeutic target in ageing and disease.

records.title: Neutrality as the null hypothesis of biological evolution
records.description: A seminal paper that showed that genome complexity in multicellular eukaryotes is shaped more by genetic drift than by natural selection.

records.title: HoT self-blinking probes for chromatin imaging
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Wang (Cosma Lab) and Zhang (Hongyan Sun Lab) describe the development of self-blinking HoT probes that are compatible with super-resolution microscopy and can be used to resolve nuclear architecture and chromatin.

records.title: Technological prominence alone does not justify leadership in SynCell governance
p53 keeps a transcription–replication balance that prevents chromothripsis
records.description: p53 loss induces global increase of transcription that causes nucleotide shortage and replication stress, thereby driving formation of DNA double-strand breaks and chromothripsis.

records.title: Mechanisms and disease relevance of DNA break repair pathway choice
records.description: This Review focuses on the choice between homologous recombination and non-homologous end joining in DNA double-strand break repair. The antagonistic roles of 53BP1 and BRCA1–BARD1, the contribution of RNA–DNA hybrids and implications for targeting repair imbalance in cancer are discussed.

records.title: A practical guide to studying genome function using single-molecule genomics
records.description: Single-molecule genomics methods are used to study the activity of regulatory factors on individual DNA molecules genome-wide, thereby enabling quantification of molecular heterogeneity and co-occurrence of regulatory events. This Expert Recommendation article provides a practical guide for adopting single-molecule genomics and outlines best practices.

records.title: PRC2–RNA interactions through the lens of bioinformatics pipeline choices
records.description: Four recent studies that have differently assessed PRC2–RNA interactions reveal key technical pitfalls underlying research in the field.

records.title: Author Correction: Mechanisms and regulation of the Hsp70 chaperone network
Towards 3D-oid models that integrate molecular, morphological and spatial cellular features
records.description: Combined analyses of cellular omics, morphology and spatial context in 3D-oids would advance tissue studies and organ engineering.

records.title: The molecular basis of transcription initiation by RNA polymerase II
records.description: Recent technological breakthroughs have transformed our understanding of how transcription initiation in eukaryotes is regulated. This Review discusses the dynamics and roles of initiation-relevant protein complexes, and how chromatin states regulate the selection of transcription start sites and transcription directionality.

records.title: CDK1 links RNA methylation to mitosis progression
records.description: During mitosis, the m 6 A methyltransferase METTL3 regulates transcription through functional interplay with the positive transcription elongation factor P-TEFb.

records.title: Charting meiotic recombination through the discovery of PRDM9
records.description: A 2010 paper identified PRDM9 as the sequence-specific regulator of meiotic recombination hotspots, showing it co-evolves with its rapidly changing binding motifs.

records.title: Mechanisms and balanced regulation of plant immunity
records.description: This Review discusses recent insights into the mechanisms of immune signalling in plants and their regulation to achieve effective defence against pathogens while preserving plant fitness. It also explores the interplay between the immune system and environmental stresses, and strategies for engineering optimal disease-resistant plants.

records.title: Towards a systems-level view of the microtubule cytoskeleton and its functions in physiology and disease
records.description: Microtubules are essential components of the cytoskeleton, yet important links between their molecular properties and organismal functions remain unresolved. In this Roadmap, Janke et al. discuss key challenges, emerging opportunities and integrative approaches to connect microtubule regulation with physiology, ageing and disease.

records.title: Not just for splicing — intronless mRNAs reveal role of nuclear speckles in nuclear export
records.description: The discovery that nuclear speckles support the nuclear export of intronless mRNAs expanded our understanding of their roles in gene regulation.

records.title: The use of homology-directed repair in a complex landscape of genome editors
records.description: This Comment discusses the uses of Cas-induced homology-directed repair in the evolving landscape of highly specialized genome editing tools.

records.title: Author Correction: Mechanisms, regulation and clinical relevance of necroptosis
Spatial-EV-seq provides a tissue map of extracellular vesicles
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Xu and Zhang (Yang lab) discuss the invention of Spatial-EV-seq, which allows researchers to spatially map extracellular vesicles in tissue slices.

records.title: Regulation and roles of mammalian mitophagy
records.description: Mitophagy contributes to cellular homeostasis through the recycling of damaged mitochondria and precise control of mitochondrial numbers. In this Review, Martens and Ganley summarize the molecular mechanisms involved in mitophagy pathways, mitophagy regulation and roles in disease.

records.title: How the discovery of mammalian regeneration shapes translational efforts
records.description: This Journal Club highlights the landmark study that provided the first evidence of regeneration in mammals, demonstrating that neonatal mice can regenerate damaged hearts and influencing regenerative medicine until today.

records.title: Shaping the anticipatory governance of synthetic cell research
records.description: Li Du advocates for stronger legal frameworks and an interdisciplinary, international approach to governing synthetic cell research.

records.title: An iron logic unites bacterial and cancer persister cells
records.description: Bacterial persisters and drug-tolerant persister cells in cancer both show reprogrammed iron homeostasis and a vulnerability to ferroptosis. Agostinis and Rodriguez propose that this iron logic is a conserved principle with implications for therapeutics development.

records.title: A call for studying the impact of multiple stressors on biological systems
records.description: Biological systems are exposed to complex combinations of environmental stressors, yet research often studies single stress conditions in isolation. In this Comment, the authors argue that studying multifactorial stress combinations is essential for understanding biological responses and improving resilience in crops, ecosystems and human health.

records.title: Mechanisms of transcription termination across the coding and noncoding loci of the genome
records.description: Transcription termination by RNA polymerase II is a tightly regulated process that involves RNA surveillance and the chromatin environment. This Review discusses the interactions between transcription termination, RNA processing, nuclear RNA decay and mRNP export, which together guide RNA fate.

records.title: Structure and function of the outer kinetochore
records.description: The kinetochore orchestrates chromosome segregation. The KMN complex, which forms the core of the outer kinetochore binds to microtubules, recruits regulators and functions as a switch for the spindle assembly checkpoint. Recent integrative imaging, biochemical and structural studies have revealed how the KMN assemblies ensure accurate chromosome segregation.

records.title: Structure and function of the centromere and inner kinetochore
records.description: The kinetochore is a macromolecular complex that assembles on centromeric chromatin and connects spindle microtubules to the chromosome. This Review discusses recent advances in determining the organization of centromeric chromatin and the complete structure and function of the inner kinetochore, which are crucial for accurate chromosome segregation.

records.title: At high noon, plants apply a condensate sunscreen
records.description: MBS1 condensates induced by high light conditions shield chloroplasts and prevent accumulation of singlet oxygen, thereby conferring tolerance without reduction in photosynthesis.

records.title: Regulation of RNA transcript elongation in metazoans and its relevance to disease
records.description: This Review discusses how transcript elongation by RNA polymerase II is regulated and how obstacles such as nucleosomes are overcome. Also discussed are the roles of transcription surveillance machineries, which ensure mRNA integrity and suppress spurious transcription, and how elongation defects contribute to diseases.

records.title: Exchange dynamics and kinetic control of gene regulation complexes
records.description: Recent evidence reveals how gene expression complexes form transient assemblies that continually exchange their subunits under kinetic control. This Perspective proposes that these dynamics form the basis of RNA processing and gene regulation.

records.title: Modulating the degree of X-inactivation escape to establish causal links to sex-biased disease
records.description: Gene escape from X-chromosome inactivation can cause sex-biased diseases. A workflow is presented to help find escape genes and experimentally manipulate their expression.

records.title: Mitochondrial tRNA biogenesis, modifications and disease relevance
records.description: Mitochondrial tRNA (mt-tRNA) biogenesis has evolved to support a degenerate mt-tRNA structure and a simplified genetic code. Liu and colleagues provide a fascinating overview of mt-tRNA biology, discuss how mt-tRNA-associated perturbations directly cause disease, and examine how emerging knowledge will lead to targeted therapeutics.

records.title: Mechanisms, regulation and clinical relevance of necroptosis
records.description: Necroptosis, a programmed cell death characterized by the formation of membrane pores and cell lysis, can be triggered by both cell-extrinsic and cell-intrinsic signals. This Review discusses mechanistic insights into necroptosis pathways mediated by receptors and by Z-nucleic acids.

records.title: Cellular and signalling mechanisms that regulate the blood–brain barrier
records.description: This Review summarizes the latest advances in blood–brain barrier (BBB) research, highlighting how emerging findings on the modulation of BBB function and heterogeneity by cellular interactions and signalling pathways might shape BBB-targeted therapeutics.

records.title: Factories, clusters, hubs, condensates — many names, one principle
records.description: Already thirty years ago, DNA replication, transcription and repair machineries were proposed to form and function in nuclear ‘factories’, later also dubbed hubs and condensates.

records.title: A demonstration that multivalent interactions drive condensate formation
records.description: A demonstration that phase separation of biomolecules is promoted by multivalent interactions, which form dynamic polymer networks with cellular functions.

records.title: Bringing CRISPR screens into tissue space
records.description: SPAC-seq combines spatial transcriptomics and CRISPR screening within the tissue context, to identify how gene perturbations influence cell states and tissues.

records.title: Human aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases as integrators of translation and cell signalling networks
records.description: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases attach amino acids to matching tRNAs to ensure accurate translation. This Review discusses new insights into their canonical and emerging non-canonical roles, including in metabolic signalling, stress responses, gene regulation and diseases.

records.title: How proteins fold
records.description: Despite advances in protein structure prediction, how proteins fold remains unclear. Understanding protein (mis)folding will require single-molecule techniques and advanced computation tools.

records.title: Reply to ‘Single-cell evidence for PANoptosome complexes’
Single-cell evidence for PANoptosome complexes
Plucking cellular ribosomes with Ribo-Tweezer
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade, Chen & Cheng (Barna lab) describe the development of Ribo-Tweezer, a method that enables the targeted degradation of individual ribosomal proteins of the cytoplasmic ribosome.

records.title: COPII meets autophagy at the ER membrane
records.description: This study shows that neutral lipids regulate endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane curvature and bendability during ER-phagy, and finds that a COPII protein helps couple ER cargo to the autophagy receptor.

records.title: Diapause presses pause on life’s developmental and ageing clock
records.description: Chi-Kuo Hu discusses a seminal 1976 paper that first described the dauer stage of Caenorhabditis elegans , in which development and ageing are paused.

records.title: Histone acetylation at the dawn of gene regulation
records.description: A 1964 study showed that histone acetylation and methylation are reversible post-transcriptional modifications that regulate transcription, linking epigenetics with metabolism.

records.title: Regulation and function of specialized membrane protrusions in intercellular communication
records.description: Tunnelling nanotubes, cytonemes and migrasomes are specialized membrane protrusions that mediate intercellular transfer of signalling molecules, organelles and other cargo. This Review discusses recent advances in their formation, architecture and transport functions, and examines their roles in development and disease.

records.title: Ancient enzymes, new biotechnology applications
records.description: Ancestral sequence reconstruction is used to resurrect extinct proteins, which often have capabilities that modern proteins lack and thus applications in biotechnology.

records.title: Programmable delivery of mitochondria to specific cell types
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Ayupov (Roska lab) describes the development of MitoCatch, a method to display protein binders on the mitochondrial surface to facilitate cell-type-specific targeting during mitochondrial transplantation.

records.title: DNA voyages through intercellular tunnels
records.description: This study shows that genomic DNA in the cytoplasm can transfer between mammalian cells through nanotube-like structures, integrate into the genome of recipient cells and support gene expression.

records.title: Tight junction structure, assembly and (dys)function
records.description: Tight junctions form essential paracellular barriers and regulate cell polarity and tissue mechanics. This Review discusses how tight junction components assemble into strand networks, and explores tight junction function in development and disease, and emerging therapeutic strategies.

records.title: Effortless immortalization of primary mouse fibroblasts
records.description: A 2003 study established that oxidative DNA damage can drive cell senescence of mouse fibroblasts, and that culturing these cells in low oxygen enables their immortalization without p53 loss.

records.title: Caveolae mechanics in cellular functions and disease
records.description: Caveolae are membrane invaginations that facilitate cell signalling and act as membrane reservoirs. This Review discusses recent insights into caveolae assembly and disassembly, their roles in mechanotransduction and how impaired caveolae mechanics contribute to human disease.

records.title: Overview of circular RNA databases and other resources
records.description: This Comment discusses databases dedicated to curating circular RNA (circRNA) information, including expression patterns, processing, interactions, translation and diseases.

records.title: Principles and mechanisms of plant acclimation to heat stress
records.description: Plants adapt to heat stress through coordinated sensing and response mechanisms driven by heat shock factors. This Review discusses recent insights into heat shock factor regulation, transcriptional reprogramming, and heat stress epigenetic memory and crosstalk with hormone signalling pathways.

records.title: Emerging evidence for a cooperative pathway of Hedgehog release
records.description: Several mechanisms have been described for the release and transport of Hedgehog morphogens. Here, Grobe and Puschmann propose a unified model in which these pathways interact synergistically.

records.title: Elucidating structure–function relationships in the mammalian nucleolus
records.description: The nucleolus is the site of ribosomal RNA synthesis and ribosome biogenesis. This Review discusses recent progress in understanding the dynamic, multilayered compartmentalization of the mammalian nucleolus, its functional importance, and how disruptions of this architecture drive cellular stresses and disease.

records.title: RNA modifications: one ring to map them all
records.description: Direct RNA sequencing by the Oxford nanopore technology enabled simultaneous mapping of different RNA modifications on the same RNA molecule and opened new avenues for studying the physiological roles of RNA modifications.

records.title: HAK-actin brings F-actin into focus in expansion microscopy
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Mercey and Lemaitre (Hamel and Guichard lab) present an actin-labelling probe compatible with ultrastructure expansion microscopy, enabling high-resolution mapping of cellular actin architecture.

records.title: New developments and applications of human organoids
records.description: Organoids are powerful tools for studying human development and disease mechanisms in vitro. This Review discusses their limitations and recent advances that increase their complexity to better mimic natural tissues, and the potential impact on therapeutic applications.

records.title: Molecular mechanisms and biotechnology applications of CRISPR–Cas12a
records.description: This Review discusses the unique features of the functionally versatile nuclease Cas12a, including allosteric regulation, structural elements controlling guide RNA maturation, target specificity, cis -cleavage and trans -cleavage activities and determinants of off-target cleavage. These features increase the applicability of Cas12a in biotechnology, therapeutics and molecular diagnostics

records.title: The PANoptosis hypothesis examined
records.description: The concept of PANoptosis describes the simultaneous activation of pyroptosis, apoptosis and necroptosis. This Comment discusses the evidence supporting this hypothesis and proposes criteria to validate PANoptosis.

records.title: The regulation, function and disease relevance of cytoplasmic tRNAs
records.description: This Review discusses the expression and maturation of human cytoplasmic tRNAs and recent insights into their regulation of translation. The authors also explore emerging roles of tRNAs in ribosome-associated quality control and in the integrated stress response and how tRNA dysregulation contributes to human pathologies.

records.title: Prevailing views of cell senescence overlook its biological complexity
records.description: David Bernard and colleagues discuss the complexity of roles of cell senescence and argue that it is crucial to study their contributions to both normal develoment and physiology, and to disease states in order to understand and manipulate cell senescence for therapeutic purposes.

records.title: In-cell chemistry enables discovery of cyclic peptide transcription factor inhibitors
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Brennan (Mason lab) describes a method that enables cyclization and screening of genetically encoded peptides to target the interaction of transcription factors with DNA.

records.title: Turing equations capture living skin patterns
records.description: Maksim Plikus discusses Alan Turing’s 1952 reaction–diffusion theory, which describes how diverse skin patterns occur, and later molecular data, from developmental mechanisms to disease, supporting the theory.

records.title: Harnessing ER-associated degradation to target transmembrane proteins
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Song and Wang describe a strategy of targeted protein degradation that harnesses endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-associated degradation machinery to degrade transmembrane proteins.

records.title: Phase separation across membranes and condensates in cell organization and function
records.description: Phase separation — the demixing of cellular components into distinct phases — shapes membrane domains and forms biomolecular condensates. This Review examines how condensates and membranes influence each other and highlights their combined importance for cellular organization and function.

records.title: Nuclear speckles of GC richness
records.description: Nuclear speckles support the splicing of levelled exon–intron architecture transcripts, and their evolution shaped genome organization in amniotes.

records.title: Programming novel intrinsically disordered proteins by directed evolution
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Ma (Dai lab) discusses the design of synthetic intrinsically disordered proteins that can be used to regulate the solubility of intracellular proteins, thereby affecting their activity.

records.title: STING signalling as a mediator between lipid metabolism and innate immunity
records.description: This Comment discusses the bidirectional interplay between STING signalling and lipid homeostasis, highlighting the emerging therapeutic relevance of this regulatory network.

records.title: Systemic epigenetic dysregulation as a driver of ageing and a therapeutic target
records.description: This Review presents a systems-level framework of how epigenetic dysregulation drives ageing, including through deterioration of nuclear architecture, dysregulation of epigenetic memory, nucleosome alterations and transcription reprogramming. These processes interact and augment gene-expression failures, and thus represent promising potential therapeutic targets.

records.title: Overcoming the challenge of preferred particle orientation in cryo-EM
records.description: Yang and Liu discuss strategies that help address particle orientation bias in cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM), and offer practical advice to tackle it.

records.title: Technologies to measure and modulate protein subcellular localization
records.description: Subcellular localization is important for protein function. This Review discusses advances in spatial subcellular proteomics, assesses the strengths and weaknesses of technologies that measure and control protein localization, and considers their potential uses in cell biology and medicine.

records.title: Overcoming cytoskeleton instability in the early embryo
records.description: Cytoplasmic partitioning in early embryos depends on microtubule asters. A study reveals that different species use distinct mechanisms to stabilize these inherently unstable structures and preserve robust cytoplasmic compartments.

records.title: Neural crest gene regulatory networks as drivers of development, diversification and disease
records.description: Neural crest cells (NCCs) are multipotent stem cells whose activation, migration and diversification are tightly controlled by gene regulatory networks that shape NCC function in vertebrate development, evolution, tissue repair and disease.

records.title: Author Correction: The hunter becomes the hunted in target-directed microRNA degradation
Precise protein expression through microRNA-mediated gene dosage compensation
records.description: Based on microRNAs, DIMMERs is a modular tool for dampening expression fluctuations of multiple proteins in a cell owing to transgene copy number variations.

records.title: The emerging importance of UBA6 in ubiquitylation and proteostasis
records.description: Ubiquitination is traditionally viewed as a one-E1 system based on UBA1, but accumulating evidence positions the related UBA6 as a distinct ubiquitin-initiating pathway that operates through unique E2 and E3 enzymes, with important functions in physiology and disease.

records.title: Probing the effects of protein glycosylation on transcription with induced-proximity tools
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Alison Mody (Woo lab) discusses a proximity-induced platform for targeted O-GlcNAcylation of proteins of interest, enabling researchers to measure the effect of O-GlcNAcylation on protein function.

records.title: Subcellular localization as a driver of protein function
records.description: Proteins can localize to multiple cellular compartments and some exhibit distinct functions depending on their location. This Review discusses the mechanisms of protein localization, the control of specialized protein functions through subcellular localization, and how mislocalization is involved in cancer, neurodegeneration and autoimmunity.

records.title: Extending microsecond time-resolved cryo-electron microscopy with laser flash melting
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Krueger (Lorenz lab) discusses laser flash melting of cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) samples for the detection of short-lived protein configurations, enabling microsecond time-resolved cryo-EM and opening new possibilities for capturing rapid structural transitions.

records.title: Evaluating evidence for UFMylation client diversity
records.description: The small ubiquitin-like modifier UFM1 is known to regulate the ribosomal subunit RPL26, but whether other bona fide substrates exist remains debated. This Comment discusses criteria for the experimental validation of UFM1 substrates.

records.title: Mechanisms and disease relevance of mitochondrial translation in humans
records.description: This Review discusses new insights into the intricate regulation of mitochondrial protein synthesis, the pathological consequences of its dysfunction in cancer and immunity, and the complexity of therapeutic targeting of mitochondrial translation.

records.title: Publisher Correction: Advancing single-cell omics and cell-based therapeutics with quantum computing
Organelles stick together through PDZD8-mediated condensate formation
records.description: Liquid–liquid phase separation of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-resident protein PDZD8 leads to the formation of biomolecular condensates that stabilize ER–mitochondria contact sites.

records.title: PIONEARing how DNA sequence composition tunes TF–nucleosome interactions
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Mariani (Bulyk Lab) describes the development of PIONEAR-Seq, a method designed to explore how genome composition influences transcription factor binding, particularly in the context of nucleosomes and other genomic elements.

records.title: Heterogeneity, dynamics and organelle interactions of lipid droplets
records.description: Lipid droplets have key roles in energy storage and lipid metabolism. This Review discusses tools used for assessing lipid droplet heterogeneity, and how their heterogeneous composition and interactions with other organelles influence physiology and contribute to disease.

records.title: The mechanistic basis and cellular functions of UFMylation
records.description: UFMylation, a ubiquitin-like modification, regulates endoplasmic reticulum-associated ribosome quality control by conjugating UFM1 to the ribosomal subunit RPL26, preserving ribosome integrity under stress. This Review explores the structural basis of UFMylation and its emerging functional breadth, and it discusses putative UFMylation substrates.

records.title: Engineered nanobodies facilitate cryo-EM studies of small proteins
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Yi and Mamalis (Gilbert and Davis labs) discuss the development of Di-Gembodies, innovative constructs designed to overcome key challenges in applying cryo-electron microscopy to small proteins that are otherwise difficult to resolve.

records.title: Inflammageing and clonal haematopoiesis interplay and their impact on human disease
records.description: Clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) is an ageing-related condition associated with a substantial fraction of leukocytes descending from a single somatically mutated haematopoietic stem cell. This Review discusses the molecular and cellular mechanisms that cause CHIP, its interplay with inflammageing, and the pathophysiological consequences and translational implications for older individuals.

records.title: Programmed ‘DNA splicing’ removes transposons from genes
records.description: A study that showed that programmed DNA elimination in somatic genomes of ciliates involves excision of intrusive, transposon-derived sequences from genes.

records.title: Progress in stem cell-based embryo models and their applications in developmental biology and biomedicine
records.description: This Review discusses recent advances and key challenges in the development of human stem cell-based embryo models, and highlights their applications in fundamental biology and translational potential while emphasizing the importance of ethical frameworks and public engagement.

records.title: Organization of replicated chromosomes by DNA loops and sister chromatid cohesion
records.description: Cohesin complexes regulate genome architecture through DNA loop extrusion and sister chromatid cohesion. The Review discusses how these two cohesin activities mediate the organization of replicated chromosomes and their segregation in mitosis and meiosis, DNA break repair, and age-related aneuploidy in oocytes.

records.title: Biology and therapeutic potential of extracellular vesicle targeting and uptake
records.description: Extracellular vesicles are released from almost all cell types and mediate intercellular communication by delivering proteins, nucleic acids and lipids. This Review examines extracellular vesicle uptake by recipient cells, their effects on signalling and their therapeutic potential and limitations.

records.title: Advancing single-cell omics and cell-based therapeutics with quantum computing
records.description: Classical computing has inherent limitations in capturing cellular dynamics. This Roadmap article discusses how recent advancements in quantum computing could overcome bottlenecks in spatiotemporal single-cell omics analyses and how it may be integrated into cell-based therapeutics.

records.title: PARP1 revisited — integrating DNA repair, replication and therapeutics
records.description: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 (PARP1) is a versatile DNA damage sensor and a major therapeutic target in cancer. This Review discusses emerging insights into how PARP1 recognizes and responds to its varied substates, and the implications of these insights on the use of PARP inhibitors.

records.title: The nucleocytoplasmic actin circuit in genome maintenance
records.description: The authors propose that nuclear actin levels are maintained through a regulatory circuit involving the DNA damage response, condensates, and transcriptional replenishment.

records.title: The integration of protein and organelle degradation systems and its pathophysiological functions
records.description: Removal of defective or excessive proteins and organelles is controlled by the ubiquitin–proteasome system and by autophagy pathways. This Review discusses the interplay between these degradation processes in response to physiological demands and cellular stresses and their pathological relevance.

records.title: Phosphatidylinositol 3,4-bisphosphate is a novel lipid helper for mitochondrial fusion
records.description: Golgi-derived vesicles that contain phosphatidylinositol 3,4-bisphosphate facilitate mitochondrial fusion at sites marked with mitofusins and endoplasmic reticulum.

records.title: Mechanisms and regulation of proteolytic DNA–protein crosslink repair
records.description: DNA–protein crosslinks (DPCs) obstruct essential chromatin processes, and their removal is crucial for genome stability. This Review discusses the origin and properties of DPCs, mechanisms of proteolytic DPC repair, and how defective DPC proteolysis contributes to genome instability, premature ageing and disease.

records.title: Similar small RNAs, different biological outcomes
records.description: Similar small RNAs in Caenorhabditis elegans pair with different Argonaute proteins, resulting in differential targeting of nucleic acids and biological outcomes.

records.description: This Review discusses how the RNA modification N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) precisely regulates eukaryotic gene expression and orchestrates cellular stress responses, metabolic homeostasis and immunity. It also explores the pathological consequences of m 6 A dysregulation in brain disorders and cancer.

records.description: The discovery of widespread expression of unstable promoter-associated transcripts has changed our understanding of genomic transcription activity.

records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Cao (Toettcher Lab) discusses the development of kinase-responsive phospho-switches that enable researchers to couple endogenous kinase signalling to activation of a synthetic protein actuator.

records.description: Large extracellular vesicle (lEV) subtypes have diverse biogenesis, cargo, functions and roles in disease. This Review article provides an overview of lEV characteristics, highlights open questions in the field and indicates how a systematic approach towards lEV characterization assisted by emerging technologies will ensure reproducibility, advancing lEV research.

records.title: Chaperone-mediated autophagy in physiological homeostasis, disease and ageing
records.description: Chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA) is a selective lysosomal degradation pathway. Recent insights into its regulation, substrate repertoire and therapeutic modulation have revealed organ-specific functions and highlighted CMA as a therapeutic target in ageing and disease.

records.description: A seminal paper that showed that genome complexity in multicellular eukaryotes is shaped more by genetic drift than by natural selection.

records.description: p53 loss induces global increase of transcription that causes nucleotide shortage and replication stress, thereby driving formation of DNA double-strand breaks and chromothripsis.

records.title: Mechanisms and disease relevance of DNA break repair pathway choice
records.description: This Review focuses on the choice between homologous recombination and non-homologous end joining in DNA double-strand break repair. The antagonistic roles of 53BP1 and BRCA1–BARD1, the contribution of RNA–DNA hybrids and implications for targeting repair imbalance in cancer are discussed.

records.title: A practical guide to studying genome function using single-molecule genomics
records.description: Single-molecule genomics methods are used to study the activity of regulatory factors on individual DNA molecules genome-wide, thereby enabling quantification of molecular heterogeneity and co-occurrence of regulatory events. This Expert Recommendation article provides a practical guide for adopting single-molecule genomics and outlines best practices.

records.title: PRC2–RNA interactions through the lens of bioinformatics pipeline choices
records.description: Four recent studies that have differently assessed PRC2–RNA interactions reveal key technical pitfalls underlying research in the field.

records.title: Author Correction: Mechanisms and regulation of the Hsp70 chaperone network
Towards 3D-oid models that integrate molecular, morphological and spatial cellular features
records.description: Combined analyses of cellular omics, morphology and spatial context in 3D-oids would advance tissue studies and organ engineering.

records.title: The molecular basis of transcription initiation by RNA polymerase II
records.description: Recent technological breakthroughs have transformed our understanding of how transcription initiation in eukaryotes is regulated. This Review discusses the dynamics and roles of initiation-relevant protein complexes, and how chromatin states regulate the selection of transcription start sites and transcription directionality.

records.title: CDK1 links RNA methylation to mitosis progression
records.description: During mitosis, the m 6 A methyltransferase METTL3 regulates transcription through functional interplay with the positive transcription elongation factor P-TEFb.

records.title: Charting meiotic recombination through the discovery of PRDM9
records.description: A 2010 paper identified PRDM9 as the sequence-specific regulator of meiotic recombination hotspots, showing it co-evolves with its rapidly changing binding motifs.

records.title: Mechanisms and balanced regulation of plant immunity
records.description: This Review discusses recent insights into the mechanisms of immune signalling in plants and their regulation to achieve effective defence against pathogens while preserving plant fitness. It also explores the interplay between the immune system and environmental stresses, and strategies for engineering optimal disease-resistant plants.

records.title: Towards a systems-level view of the microtubule cytoskeleton and its functions in physiology and disease
records.description: Microtubules are essential components of the cytoskeleton, yet important links between their molecular properties and organismal functions remain unresolved. In this Roadmap, Janke et al. discuss key challenges, emerging opportunities and integrative approaches to connect microtubule regulation with physiology, ageing and disease.

records.title: Not just for splicing — intronless mRNAs reveal role of nuclear speckles in nuclear export
records.description: The discovery that nuclear speckles support the nuclear export of intronless mRNAs expanded our understanding of their roles in gene regulation.

records.title: The use of homology-directed repair in a complex landscape of genome editors
records.description: This Comment discusses the uses of Cas-induced homology-directed repair in the evolving landscape of highly specialized genome editing tools.

records.title: Author Correction: Mechanisms, regulation and clinical relevance of necroptosis
Spatial-EV-seq provides a tissue map of extracellular vesicles
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Xu and Zhang (Yang lab) discuss the invention of Spatial-EV-seq, which allows researchers to spatially map extracellular vesicles in tissue slices.

records.title: Regulation and roles of mammalian mitophagy
records.description: Mitophagy contributes to cellular homeostasis through the recycling of damaged mitochondria and precise control of mitochondrial numbers. In this Review, Martens and Ganley summarize the molecular mechanisms involved in mitophagy pathways, mitophagy regulation and roles in disease.

records.title: How the discovery of mammalian regeneration shapes translational efforts
records.description: This Journal Club highlights the landmark study that provided the first evidence of regeneration in mammals, demonstrating that neonatal mice can regenerate damaged hearts and influencing regenerative medicine until today.

records.title: Shaping the anticipatory governance of synthetic cell research
records.description: Li Du advocates for stronger legal frameworks and an interdisciplinary, international approach to governing synthetic cell research.

records.title: An iron logic unites bacterial and cancer persister cells
records.description: Bacterial persisters and drug-tolerant persister cells in cancer both show reprogrammed iron homeostasis and a vulnerability to ferroptosis. Agostinis and Rodriguez propose that this iron logic is a conserved principle with implications for therapeutics development.

records.title: A call for studying the impact of multiple stressors on biological systems
records.description: Biological systems are exposed to complex combinations of environmental stressors, yet research often studies single stress conditions in isolation. In this Comment, the authors argue that studying multifactorial stress combinations is essential for understanding biological responses and improving resilience in crops, ecosystems and human health.

records.title: Mechanisms of transcription termination across the coding and noncoding loci of the genome
records.description: Transcription termination by RNA polymerase II is a tightly regulated process that involves RNA surveillance and the chromatin environment. This Review discusses the interactions between transcription termination, RNA processing, nuclear RNA decay and mRNP export, which together guide RNA fate.

records.title: Structure and function of the outer kinetochore
records.description: The kinetochore orchestrates chromosome segregation. The KMN complex, which forms the core of the outer kinetochore binds to microtubules, recruits regulators and functions as a switch for the spindle assembly checkpoint. Recent integrative imaging, biochemical and structural studies have revealed how the KMN assemblies ensure accurate chromosome segregation.

records.title: Structure and function of the centromere and inner kinetochore
records.description: The kinetochore is a macromolecular complex that assembles on centromeric chromatin and connects spindle microtubules to the chromosome. This Review discusses recent advances in determining the organization of centromeric chromatin and the complete structure and function of the inner kinetochore, which are crucial for accurate chromosome segregation.

records.title: At high noon, plants apply a condensate sunscreen
records.description: MBS1 condensates induced by high light conditions shield chloroplasts and prevent accumulation of singlet oxygen, thereby conferring tolerance without reduction in photosynthesis.

records.title: Regulation of RNA transcript elongation in metazoans and its relevance to disease
records.description: This Review discusses how transcript elongation by RNA polymerase II is regulated and how obstacles such as nucleosomes are overcome. Also discussed are the roles of transcription surveillance machineries, which ensure mRNA integrity and suppress spurious transcription, and how elongation defects contribute to diseases.

records.title: Exchange dynamics and kinetic control of gene regulation complexes
records.description: Recent evidence reveals how gene expression complexes form transient assemblies that continually exchange their subunits under kinetic control. This Perspective proposes that these dynamics form the basis of RNA processing and gene regulation.

records.title: Modulating the degree of X-inactivation escape to establish causal links to sex-biased disease
records.description: Gene escape from X-chromosome inactivation can cause sex-biased diseases. A workflow is presented to help find escape genes and experimentally manipulate their expression.

records.title: Mitochondrial tRNA biogenesis, modifications and disease relevance
records.description: Mitochondrial tRNA (mt-tRNA) biogenesis has evolved to support a degenerate mt-tRNA structure and a simplified genetic code. Liu and colleagues provide a fascinating overview of mt-tRNA biology, discuss how mt-tRNA-associated perturbations directly cause disease, and examine how emerging knowledge will lead to targeted therapeutics.

records.title: Mechanisms, regulation and clinical relevance of necroptosis
records.description: Necroptosis, a programmed cell death characterized by the formation of membrane pores and cell lysis, can be triggered by both cell-extrinsic and cell-intrinsic signals. This Review discusses mechanistic insights into necroptosis pathways mediated by receptors and by Z-nucleic acids.

records.title: Cellular and signalling mechanisms that regulate the blood–brain barrier
records.description: This Review summarizes the latest advances in blood–brain barrier (BBB) research, highlighting how emerging findings on the modulation of BBB function and heterogeneity by cellular interactions and signalling pathways might shape BBB-targeted therapeutics.

records.title: Factories, clusters, hubs, condensates — many names, one principle
records.description: Already thirty years ago, DNA replication, transcription and repair machineries were proposed to form and function in nuclear ‘factories’, later also dubbed hubs and condensates.

records.title: A demonstration that multivalent interactions drive condensate formation
records.description: A demonstration that phase separation of biomolecules is promoted by multivalent interactions, which form dynamic polymer networks with cellular functions.

records.title: Bringing CRISPR screens into tissue space
records.description: SPAC-seq combines spatial transcriptomics and CRISPR screening within the tissue context, to identify how gene perturbations influence cell states and tissues.

records.title: Human aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases as integrators of translation and cell signalling networks
records.description: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases attach amino acids to matching tRNAs to ensure accurate translation. This Review discusses new insights into their canonical and emerging non-canonical roles, including in metabolic signalling, stress responses, gene regulation and diseases.

records.title: How proteins fold
records.description: Despite advances in protein structure prediction, how proteins fold remains unclear. Understanding protein (mis)folding will require single-molecule techniques and advanced computation tools.

records.title: Reply to ‘Single-cell evidence for PANoptosome complexes’
Single-cell evidence for PANoptosome complexes
Plucking cellular ribosomes with Ribo-Tweezer
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade, Chen & Cheng (Barna lab) describe the development of Ribo-Tweezer, a method that enables the targeted degradation of individual ribosomal proteins of the cytoplasmic ribosome.

records.title: COPII meets autophagy at the ER membrane
records.description: This study shows that neutral lipids regulate endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane curvature and bendability during ER-phagy, and finds that a COPII protein helps couple ER cargo to the autophagy receptor.

records.title: Diapause presses pause on life’s developmental and ageing clock
records.description: Chi-Kuo Hu discusses a seminal 1976 paper that first described the dauer stage of Caenorhabditis elegans , in which development and ageing are paused.

records.title: Histone acetylation at the dawn of gene regulation
records.description: A 1964 study showed that histone acetylation and methylation are reversible post-transcriptional modifications that regulate transcription, linking epigenetics with metabolism.

records.title: Regulation and function of specialized membrane protrusions in intercellular communication
records.description: Tunnelling nanotubes, cytonemes and migrasomes are specialized membrane protrusions that mediate intercellular transfer of signalling molecules, organelles and other cargo. This Review discusses recent advances in their formation, architecture and transport functions, and examines their roles in development and disease.

records.title: Ancient enzymes, new biotechnology applications
records.description: Ancestral sequence reconstruction is used to resurrect extinct proteins, which often have capabilities that modern proteins lack and thus applications in biotechnology.

records.title: Programmable delivery of mitochondria to specific cell types
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Ayupov (Roska lab) describes the development of MitoCatch, a method to display protein binders on the mitochondrial surface to facilitate cell-type-specific targeting during mitochondrial transplantation.

records.title: DNA voyages through intercellular tunnels
records.description: This study shows that genomic DNA in the cytoplasm can transfer between mammalian cells through nanotube-like structures, integrate into the genome of recipient cells and support gene expression.

records.title: Tight junction structure, assembly and (dys)function
records.description: Tight junctions form essential paracellular barriers and regulate cell polarity and tissue mechanics. This Review discusses how tight junction components assemble into strand networks, and explores tight junction function in development and disease, and emerging therapeutic strategies.

records.title: Effortless immortalization of primary mouse fibroblasts
records.description: A 2003 study established that oxidative DNA damage can drive cell senescence of mouse fibroblasts, and that culturing these cells in low oxygen enables their immortalization without p53 loss.

records.title: Caveolae mechanics in cellular functions and disease
records.description: Caveolae are membrane invaginations that facilitate cell signalling and act as membrane reservoirs. This Review discusses recent insights into caveolae assembly and disassembly, their roles in mechanotransduction and how impaired caveolae mechanics contribute to human disease.

records.title: Overview of circular RNA databases and other resources
records.description: This Comment discusses databases dedicated to curating circular RNA (circRNA) information, including expression patterns, processing, interactions, translation and diseases.

records.title: Principles and mechanisms of plant acclimation to heat stress
records.description: Plants adapt to heat stress through coordinated sensing and response mechanisms driven by heat shock factors. This Review discusses recent insights into heat shock factor regulation, transcriptional reprogramming, and heat stress epigenetic memory and crosstalk with hormone signalling pathways.

records.title: Emerging evidence for a cooperative pathway of Hedgehog release
records.description: Several mechanisms have been described for the release and transport of Hedgehog morphogens. Here, Grobe and Puschmann propose a unified model in which these pathways interact synergistically.

records.title: Elucidating structure–function relationships in the mammalian nucleolus
records.description: The nucleolus is the site of ribosomal RNA synthesis and ribosome biogenesis. This Review discusses recent progress in understanding the dynamic, multilayered compartmentalization of the mammalian nucleolus, its functional importance, and how disruptions of this architecture drive cellular stresses and disease.

records.title: RNA modifications: one ring to map them all
records.description: Direct RNA sequencing by the Oxford nanopore technology enabled simultaneous mapping of different RNA modifications on the same RNA molecule and opened new avenues for studying the physiological roles of RNA modifications.

records.title: HAK-actin brings F-actin into focus in expansion microscopy
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Mercey and Lemaitre (Hamel and Guichard lab) present an actin-labelling probe compatible with ultrastructure expansion microscopy, enabling high-resolution mapping of cellular actin architecture.

records.title: New developments and applications of human organoids
records.description: Organoids are powerful tools for studying human development and disease mechanisms in vitro. This Review discusses their limitations and recent advances that increase their complexity to better mimic natural tissues, and the potential impact on therapeutic applications.

records.title: Molecular mechanisms and biotechnology applications of CRISPR–Cas12a
records.description: This Review discusses the unique features of the functionally versatile nuclease Cas12a, including allosteric regulation, structural elements controlling guide RNA maturation, target specificity, cis -cleavage and trans -cleavage activities and determinants of off-target cleavage. These features increase the applicability of Cas12a in biotechnology, therapeutics and molecular diagnostics

records.title: The PANoptosis hypothesis examined
records.description: The concept of PANoptosis describes the simultaneous activation of pyroptosis, apoptosis and necroptosis. This Comment discusses the evidence supporting this hypothesis and proposes criteria to validate PANoptosis.

records.title: The regulation, function and disease relevance of cytoplasmic tRNAs
records.description: This Review discusses the expression and maturation of human cytoplasmic tRNAs and recent insights into their regulation of translation. The authors also explore emerging roles of tRNAs in ribosome-associated quality control and in the integrated stress response and how tRNA dysregulation contributes to human pathologies.

records.title: Prevailing views of cell senescence overlook its biological complexity
records.description: David Bernard and colleagues discuss the complexity of roles of cell senescence and argue that it is crucial to study their contributions to both normal develoment and physiology, and to disease states in order to understand and manipulate cell senescence for therapeutic purposes.

records.title: In-cell chemistry enables discovery of cyclic peptide transcription factor inhibitors
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Brennan (Mason lab) describes a method that enables cyclization and screening of genetically encoded peptides to target the interaction of transcription factors with DNA.

records.title: Turing equations capture living skin patterns
records.description: Maksim Plikus discusses Alan Turing’s 1952 reaction–diffusion theory, which describes how diverse skin patterns occur, and later molecular data, from developmental mechanisms to disease, supporting the theory.

records.title: Harnessing ER-associated degradation to target transmembrane proteins
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Song and Wang describe a strategy of targeted protein degradation that harnesses endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-associated degradation machinery to degrade transmembrane proteins.

records.title: Phase separation across membranes and condensates in cell organization and function
records.description: Phase separation — the demixing of cellular components into distinct phases — shapes membrane domains and forms biomolecular condensates. This Review examines how condensates and membranes influence each other and highlights their combined importance for cellular organization and function.

records.title: Nuclear speckles of GC richness
records.description: Nuclear speckles support the splicing of levelled exon–intron architecture transcripts, and their evolution shaped genome organization in amniotes.

records.title: Programming novel intrinsically disordered proteins by directed evolution
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Ma (Dai lab) discusses the design of synthetic intrinsically disordered proteins that can be used to regulate the solubility of intracellular proteins, thereby affecting their activity.

records.title: STING signalling as a mediator between lipid metabolism and innate immunity
records.description: This Comment discusses the bidirectional interplay between STING signalling and lipid homeostasis, highlighting the emerging therapeutic relevance of this regulatory network.

records.title: Systemic epigenetic dysregulation as a driver of ageing and a therapeutic target
records.description: This Review presents a systems-level framework of how epigenetic dysregulation drives ageing, including through deterioration of nuclear architecture, dysregulation of epigenetic memory, nucleosome alterations and transcription reprogramming. These processes interact and augment gene-expression failures, and thus represent promising potential therapeutic targets.

records.title: Overcoming the challenge of preferred particle orientation in cryo-EM
records.description: Yang and Liu discuss strategies that help address particle orientation bias in cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM), and offer practical advice to tackle it.

records.title: Technologies to measure and modulate protein subcellular localization
records.description: Subcellular localization is important for protein function. This Review discusses advances in spatial subcellular proteomics, assesses the strengths and weaknesses of technologies that measure and control protein localization, and considers their potential uses in cell biology and medicine.

records.title: Overcoming cytoskeleton instability in the early embryo
records.description: Cytoplasmic partitioning in early embryos depends on microtubule asters. A study reveals that different species use distinct mechanisms to stabilize these inherently unstable structures and preserve robust cytoplasmic compartments.

records.title: Neural crest gene regulatory networks as drivers of development, diversification and disease
records.description: Neural crest cells (NCCs) are multipotent stem cells whose activation, migration and diversification are tightly controlled by gene regulatory networks that shape NCC function in vertebrate development, evolution, tissue repair and disease.

records.title: Author Correction: The hunter becomes the hunted in target-directed microRNA degradation
Precise protein expression through microRNA-mediated gene dosage compensation
records.description: Based on microRNAs, DIMMERs is a modular tool for dampening expression fluctuations of multiple proteins in a cell owing to transgene copy number variations.

records.title: The emerging importance of UBA6 in ubiquitylation and proteostasis
records.description: Ubiquitination is traditionally viewed as a one-E1 system based on UBA1, but accumulating evidence positions the related UBA6 as a distinct ubiquitin-initiating pathway that operates through unique E2 and E3 enzymes, with important functions in physiology and disease.

records.title: Probing the effects of protein glycosylation on transcription with induced-proximity tools
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Alison Mody (Woo lab) discusses a proximity-induced platform for targeted O-GlcNAcylation of proteins of interest, enabling researchers to measure the effect of O-GlcNAcylation on protein function.

records.title: Subcellular localization as a driver of protein function
records.description: Proteins can localize to multiple cellular compartments and some exhibit distinct functions depending on their location. This Review discusses the mechanisms of protein localization, the control of specialized protein functions through subcellular localization, and how mislocalization is involved in cancer, neurodegeneration and autoimmunity.

records.title: Extending microsecond time-resolved cryo-electron microscopy with laser flash melting
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Krueger (Lorenz lab) discusses laser flash melting of cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) samples for the detection of short-lived protein configurations, enabling microsecond time-resolved cryo-EM and opening new possibilities for capturing rapid structural transitions.

records.title: Evaluating evidence for UFMylation client diversity
records.description: The small ubiquitin-like modifier UFM1 is known to regulate the ribosomal subunit RPL26, but whether other bona fide substrates exist remains debated. This Comment discusses criteria for the experimental validation of UFM1 substrates.

records.title: Mechanisms and disease relevance of mitochondrial translation in humans
records.description: This Review discusses new insights into the intricate regulation of mitochondrial protein synthesis, the pathological consequences of its dysfunction in cancer and immunity, and the complexity of therapeutic targeting of mitochondrial translation.

records.title: Publisher Correction: Advancing single-cell omics and cell-based therapeutics with quantum computing
Organelles stick together through PDZD8-mediated condensate formation
records.description: Liquid–liquid phase separation of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-resident protein PDZD8 leads to the formation of biomolecular condensates that stabilize ER–mitochondria contact sites.

records.title: PIONEARing how DNA sequence composition tunes TF–nucleosome interactions
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Mariani (Bulyk Lab) describes the development of PIONEAR-Seq, a method designed to explore how genome composition influences transcription factor binding, particularly in the context of nucleosomes and other genomic elements.

records.title: Heterogeneity, dynamics and organelle interactions of lipid droplets
records.description: Lipid droplets have key roles in energy storage and lipid metabolism. This Review discusses tools used for assessing lipid droplet heterogeneity, and how their heterogeneous composition and interactions with other organelles influence physiology and contribute to disease.

records.title: The mechanistic basis and cellular functions of UFMylation
records.description: UFMylation, a ubiquitin-like modification, regulates endoplasmic reticulum-associated ribosome quality control by conjugating UFM1 to the ribosomal subunit RPL26, preserving ribosome integrity under stress. This Review explores the structural basis of UFMylation and its emerging functional breadth, and it discusses putative UFMylation substrates.

records.title: Engineered nanobodies facilitate cryo-EM studies of small proteins
records.description: In this Tools of the Trade article, Yi and Mamalis (Gilbert and Davis labs) discuss the development of Di-Gembodies, innovative constructs designed to overcome key challenges in applying cryo-electron microscopy to small proteins that are otherwise difficult to resolve.

records.title: Inflammageing and clonal haematopoiesis interplay and their impact on human disease
records.description: Clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) is an ageing-related condition associated with a substantial fraction of leukocytes descending from a single somatically mutated haematopoietic stem cell. This Review discusses the molecular and cellular mechanisms that cause CHIP, its interplay with inflammageing, and the pathophysiological consequences and translational implications for older individuals.

records.title: Programmed ‘DNA splicing’ removes transposons from genes
records.description: A study that showed that programmed DNA elimination in somatic genomes of ciliates involves excision of intrusive, transposon-derived sequences from genes.

records.title: Progress in stem cell-based embryo models and their applications in developmental biology and biomedicine
records.description: This Review discusses recent advances and key challenges in the development of human stem cell-based embryo models, and highlights their applications in fundamental biology and translational potential while emphasizing the importance of ethical frameworks and public engagement.

records.title: Organization of replicated chromosomes by DNA loops and sister chromatid cohesion
records.description: Cohesin complexes regulate genome architecture through DNA loop extrusion and sister chromatid cohesion. The Review discusses how these two cohesin activities mediate the organization of replicated chromosomes and their segregation in mitosis and meiosis, DNA break repair, and age-related aneuploidy in oocytes.

records.title: Biology and therapeutic potential of extracellular vesicle targeting and uptake
records.description: Extracellular vesicles are released from almost all cell types and mediate intercellular communication by delivering proteins, nucleic acids and lipids. This Review examines extracellular vesicle uptake by recipient cells, their effects on signalling and their therapeutic potential and limitations.

records.title: Advancing single-cell omics and cell-based therapeutics with quantum computing
records.description: Classical computing has inherent limitations in capturing cellular dynamics. This Roadmap article discusses how recent advancements in quantum computing could overcome bottlenecks in spatiotemporal single-cell omics analyses and how it may be integrated into cell-based therapeutics.
